# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 12, 2026
**Re:** Noubin Auto Exchange, LLC / Trupel Lanecast, Inc.: Review of MSA and Related Documents

**Privileged & Confidential: Attorney Work Product**

---

## 1. Executive Summary

I reviewed all eight documents in the folder:

- **D1** Master Services Agreement ("MSA")
- **D2** Order Form No. 1
- **D3** Service Level Schedule ("SLS")
- **D4** Statement of Work ("SOW")
- **D5** Side Letter dated October 26, 2026
- **D6** Term Sheet dated February 20, 2026
- **D7** Ostrander lot-sweeping agreement
- **D8** Trupel's certificate of insurance

D7 and D8 do not bear on the Trupel issues, as explained in Section 4.

I found six issues. Three of them only appear when two documents are read together. The precedence clause drives most of them. **MSA §1.3** ranks the documents in "descending order of precedence": (a) Side Letter, (b) SOW, (c) Order Form, (d) SLS, (e) MSA. It then states expressly that "if there is a conflict between the Statement of Work and this MSA, **the Statement of Work shall prevail**." The MSA sits at the bottom of the hierarchy. Trupel's SOW therefore overrides the MSA's protections wherever the two conflict.

### Items requiring urgent attention

| # | Issue | Why urgent |
|---|---|---|
| **URGENT 1** | Chronic Failure termination notice was untimely (Issue 4) | The 15-day window closed **October 15, 2026**. Noubin's notice is dated **October 19, 2026**, four days late. A possible **fresh** Chronic Failure window (August–October 2026) may close **November 15, 2026**, which is three days from today. Trupel's remediation plan is due tomorrow, **November 13, 2026**. |
| **URGENT 2** | Georgia law and forum (Issue 1) | The live termination dispute is a "claim relating to the Services." Under the SOW it would go to Fulton County, Georgia, under Georgia law. If litigation is contemplated, this needs a strategy now. |
| **URGENT 3** | Overbroad exclusivity (Issue 5) | Noubin's existing transport, title, inspection and arbitration vendors may already put it in breach of MSA §3.4. |

The renewal trap (Issue 2) does not bite until 2030. It should still be fixed in the current negotiation, while Trupel wants to keep the relationship.

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: Georgia law and forum override the Delaware choice through the precedence clause

**Where:**
- SOW (D4) §10.1–10.2
- MSA (D1) §1.3, read with MSA §14.1–14.2

**What the documents say:**
- MSA §14.1 selects **Delaware law**.
- MSA §14.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to the **state or federal courts in New Castle County, Delaware**. This matches Term Sheet §11.
- SOW §10.1 provides that the SOW "and all claims arising out of or relating to the Services performed under it are governed by... **the laws of the State of Georgia**."
- SOW §10.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to "the state and federal courts located in **Fulton County, Georgia**."
- MSA §1.3 says the SOW prevails over the MSA in a conflict.

Two further drafting points make this worse:
- MSA §14 is limited to disputes relating to "this MSA."
- SOW §10 reaches all claims relating to "the Services," which the MSA defines (§1.1) to include the Platform itself.

**Why it matters to Noubin:**
- The disputes most likely to arise would be heard in Trupel's home forum, under Trupel's home law. These are platform outages, SLA failures, condition-report errors and the pending Chronic Failure termination.
- Noubin also faces **split proceedings**. Claims about data, confidentiality or payment under the MSA would go to Delaware, while service claims would go to Georgia. That creates duplicative litigation and a risk of inconsistent results.
- This was not the deal. Term Sheet §11 provided for Delaware law and a New Castle County forum with no exceptions.
- Side Letter §6.2 makes the Side Letter itself subject to MSA §14. Even so, the underlying termination dispute is plainly a Services claim.

**Recommendation:**
- Delete SOW §10 entirely.
- Amend MSA §1.3 so that MSA §§9, 11, 14 and 15 control notwithstanding anything in any SOW, Order Form or Side Letter, unless the lower document expressly references and amends the specific MSA section.
- Broaden MSA §14.1–14.2 to cover "the Agreement and all claims arising out of or relating to the Agreement or the Services."
- **Near term:** before any filing on the termination dispute, assess whether to file first in Delaware. Note that the SOW forum clause cuts against this. Also consider whether a Side Letter amendment could fix the forum now, since a Side Letter outranks the SOW.

---

### Issue 2: Automatic five-year renewals with a single 30-day opt-out window

**Where:**
- MSA (D1) §12.2
- Order Form (D2) §3.1–3.2

**What the documents say:**
- MSA §12.2 renews the Agreement automatically "for successive renewal terms, **each equal in length to the Initial Term**."
- Non-renewal notice is effective only if delivered "**not earlier than two hundred ten (210) days** and not later than one hundred eighty (180) days" before expiry.
- The MSA does not state the length of the Initial Term. Order Form §3 sets it at **sixty (60) months** from April 1, 2026.

**Why it matters to Noubin:**
- Read together, each renewal is a **five-year renewal**.
- The Initial Term runs to about March 31, 2031. The only opt-out window is roughly **September 2 – October 2, 2030**. The exact dates should be confirmed against MSA §13 notice mechanics.
- A notice sent one day early is as ineffective as one sent one day late.
- If Noubin misses the window, it is locked in through about March 2036, with platform exclusivity across every site (see Issue 5).
- Term Sheet §5.2 left renewal "to be agreed." Noubin never agreed to five-year evergreen terms.
- Order Form §4.5 has no minimum commitment, which softens the economic exposure. The exclusivity lock-in is the real cost.

**Recommendation:**
- Amend §12.2 so that renewal terms are **one year**, or require mutual written agreement to renew.
- Allow non-renewal notice **at any time** up to, for example, 60–90 days before expiry. There should be no "not earlier than" floor.
- Consider adding termination for convenience during any Renewal Term.
- Docket the 2030 window now as a backstop in case the amendment is not obtained.

---

### Issue 3: Uncapped indemnity extended to Trupel's own condition reports

**Where:**
- SOW (D4) §6.2 (with the "Vehicle Disclosures" definition in SOW §2)
- MSA (D1) §9.2 and §11.3

**What the documents say:**
- MSA §9.2 requires Noubin to defend and indemnify Trupel against third-party claims arising from "**Consignor Content**."
- The MSA defines Consignor Content (§1.1) as content supplied by Noubin or a Consignor.
- MSA §11.3 provides that the 12-month-fees cap in §11.1 and the consequential-damages exclusion in §11.2 "**shall not apply to either party's obligations under Section 9**."
- SOW §6.2 then redefines Consignor Content, for purposes of MSA §9.2, to include "all Vehicle Disclosures displayed on the Platform, **including condition reports prepared by Trupel Inspectors**."
- Under SOW §2, "Vehicle Disclosures" also includes odometer statements, title status and brand information, and frame and structural damage disclosures.
- Because the SOW prevails (MSA §1.3), the SOW definition controls.

**Why it matters to Noubin:**
- Noubin would owe Trupel an **uncapped indemnity**, including defense costs, for buyer claims caused by **Trupel's own inspectors' errors**. Examples are missed frame damage, a misread odometer, or an undisclosed flood or title brand.
- These are exactly the claims that arise in wholesale auction arbitration and in dealer litigation, including odometer and title-brand claims that can carry statutory damages.
- In effect, Noubin insures Trupel's negligence without limit. Meanwhile Trupel's own liability to Noubin is capped at 12 months' fees.
- This reverses Term Sheet §10.3. Under the term sheet, Noubin indemnifies only for "vehicle content supplied by Noubin or its consignors."
- It also undercuts the value of the condition-report service, and of Trupel's $5M tech E&O policy (D8), which should be responding to these claims.

**Recommendation:**
- Strike SOW §6.2.
- Amend the Consignor Content definition to **exclude** Condition Reports and any content prepared or altered by Trupel or its subcontractors.
- Add a Trupel indemnity in MSA §9.1 for third-party claims arising from Condition Report errors or Trupel Inspector negligence.
- Bring Noubin's §9.2 indemnity under a cap, or a separate super-cap, while keeping Trupel's IP and data-breach indemnities uncapped.
- As in Issue 1, put the core MSA protections beyond override by the SOW.

---

### Issue 4 (URGENT): Chronic Failure termination notice delivered after the 15-day window

**Where:**
- Service Level Schedule (D3) §6.1–6.2
- Side Letter (D5) §2.1, §2.3–2.5 and §5

**What the documents say:**
- SLS §6.2 allows termination on a Chronic Failure, meaning three consecutive months below the 99.5% Monthly Availability Service Level.
- The notice "must be delivered **within fifteen (15) days after the end of the third consecutive** Measurement Period."
- Side Letter §2.1 records that availability failed in July (99.1%), August (98.6%) and September (98.9%) 2026.
- Side Letter §2.3 records Noubin's notice "dated **October 19, 2026**," effective January 15, 2027.
- In §2.4, Trupel "disputes the timeliness" of the notice.
- In §2.5, Noubin maintains that the notice is valid.
- Under §5.1–5.2, neither party waives any right, and accepting credits is not an admission.

**Analysis:**
- The third failing month ended September 30, 2026, so the window closed **October 15, 2026**.
- Notice was delivered October 19, 2026, which is **four days late**.
- Notice is effective on delivery or transmission (MSA §13.1), and Trupel acknowledges receipt on October 19. No earlier-delivery argument appears available.
- On the face of the documents, the termination right under SLS §6.2 has likely lapsed. Noubin's stated position is weak unless facts outside the folder support an earlier notice or a waiver by Trupel.
- MSA §16.3 says no waiver is effective unless it is in writing.

**Why it matters to Noubin:**
- If the notice is ineffective, the Agreement does **not** end on January 15, 2027. Noubin remains bound by the 60-month term and the exclusivity.
- If Noubin stops performing or moves to a replacement vendor, Trupel may treat that as a repudiation.
- Noubin would also lose the clean-exit benefits of SLS §6.3: no termination charges and free transition assistance.

**Recommendations, in priority order:**

1. **Check for a fresh Chronic Failure immediately.**
   - Chronic Failure is any three *consecutive* failing months, so it can roll forward.
   - If **October 2026** availability was also below 99.5%, then August, September and October are a new set of three consecutive failures.
   - On that basis a new 15-day window runs to **November 15, 2026**, which falls on a Sunday.
   - Trupel's October service level report is due within 10 business days of month-end (SLS §7.1), which is around now.
   - Obtain October monitoring data under SLS §7.2 and Side Letter §4.3.
   - If availability failed, serve a **protective Chronic Failure notice** by email with courier copy under MSA §13 **no later than Friday, November 13, 2026**. The notice should reference the August–October periods and expressly preserve the October 19 notice.
2. **Seek a written extension or waiver from Trupel.** Ask Trupel to confirm in writing that the October 19 notice is timely, or to extend the window. A Side Letter amendment is the ideal vehicle because it sits at the top of the MSA §1.3 hierarchy.
3. **Preserve alternative grounds.**
   - Termination for material breach under MSA §12.3 requires 30 days' notice and a cure period. Possible breaches include repeated failure to meet the 15-minute failover requirement in SOW §8.2 and the release-testing defects.
   - SLS §5.5 confirms that service credits do not limit Noubin's §6 or §12.3 rights.
   - Consider serving a breach notice now so that the cure period runs in parallel.
4. **Do not treat credits as the sole remedy.** Confirm the Side Letter's §5 reservation is preserved in any countersignature, and do not sign anything that recharacterizes the credits as full satisfaction. Review whether Noubin has countersigned the October 26 Side Letter. Because it outranks the SOW, its wording matters.
5. **Keep performing** under Side Letter §2.6 until the dispute is resolved. Do not assume a January 15, 2027 exit when planning vendor transitions.
6. Review Trupel's remediation plan, due **November 13, 2026** under Side Letter §4.1, for admissions that support a breach claim.

---

### Issue 5 (URGENT): Exclusivity far broader than the term-sheet deal

**Where:**
- MSA (D1) §3.4, read with the §1.1 definitions of "Auction Technology Services," "Noubin Facility" and "Affiliate"
- Compare Term Sheet (D6) §4

**What the documents say:**
- MSA §3.4 bars Noubin and its Affiliates from procuring "**any Auction Technology Services**" from anyone but Trupel at any Noubin Facility. It also bars Noubin from developing substitute services in-house.
- "Auction Technology Services" covers simulcast bidding, condition reports and inspections, transport scheduling and logistics, title processing and document management, and post-sale arbitration management, "together with any similar or related service."
- "Noubin Facility" covers any site "owned, operated or managed by Noubin or any of its **Affiliates**, wherever located, whether now existing or later acquired or established."

**Why it matters to Noubin:**
- Term Sheet §4 limited exclusivity to "online simulcast bidding **only**, at the **New Castle, Elkton and Salisbury** auction sites."
- Term Sheet §4.2 expressly excluded condition reports, transport, title and arbitration management, and stated that existing vendor arrangements "will continue unaffected."
- Term Sheet §4.3 expressly excluded after-acquired sites.
- As signed, §3.4 creates the following problems:
  - Noubin's **existing transport and title vendors may already be in breach territory**.
  - Any acquisition of another auction, or any affiliate's auction, nationwide would be locked into Trupel for all services.
  - Noubin cannot build its own tools.
  - Combined with Issue 2, this could last until 2036.
- The term sheet is non-binding (§13.1). It remains strong evidence of the agreed deal and useful negotiating leverage, but it does not by itself override the signed MSA.

**Recommendation:**
- Narrow §3.4 to online simulcast bidding at the three Covered Sites listed in Order Form §2.1.
- Exclude Affiliates and after-acquired sites.
- Delete the in-house development bar, or limit it to simulcast.
- Add a carve-out confirming that existing vendor arrangements continue.
- **Near term:** inventory Noubin's current third-party auction-technology vendors to assess exposure. Avoid new vendor commitments until §3.4 is fixed.

---

### Issue 6: Trupel can assign freely, including to a competitor

**Where:** MSA (D1) §15.2, compared with §15.1

**What the documents say:**
- Noubin may not assign without Trupel's prior written consent, including by merger or operation of law (§15.1).
- By contrast, "Trupel may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, **without Noubin's consent** to any person, upon written notice to Noubin" (§15.2).

**Why it matters to Noubin:**
- Nothing prevents assignment to a **competing auction operator** or its affiliate.
- The assignee would hold Noubin's Customer Data, including dealer buyer lists, consignor data, bid histories and pricing (MSA §1.1). That is Noubin's most valuable commercial information.
- Noubin would remain bound by exclusivity and the long term.
- Partial assignment could also split the platform and condition-report services across different providers.
- The restriction on Noubin's own assignment, which covers mergers, could also impede a sale of Noubin's business.

**Recommendation:**
- Require Noubin's prior written consent for any assignment by Trupel, with a narrow exception for a successor to substantially all of Trupel's business that is **not a competitor** of Noubin and that assumes the Agreement in writing.
- Prohibit partial assignment.
- Give Noubin a right to terminate without penalty, with free transition assistance and data return under MSA §5.4, on any assignment or change of control that results in a competitor controlling Trupel.
- Make §15 mutual, including a successor-in-merger exception for Noubin.

---

## 3. Fact Check of Key Terms

- **Effective Date:** April 1, 2026 (D1 preamble; D2 §1). **Go-Live:** June 1, 2026 (D4 §4.1).
- **Fees:**
  - $42 per vehicle sold through simulcast (D2 §4.1)
  - $38 per Condition Report (D4 §7.1)
  - No minimum commitment (D2 §4.5)
- **Service Level:** 99.5% Monthly Availability (D3 §2.1). Credits are capped at 40% of Monthly Platform Fees (D3 §5.3).
- **Liability cap:** fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months (D1 §11.1), subject to the §11.3 carve-outs discussed in Issue 3.

## 4. Documents Not Raising Issues

- **Ostrander lot-sweeping agreement (D7):** an unrelated vendor agreement. It has no bearing on the Trupel relationship. Note that lot sweeping falls outside even the broad "Auction Technology Services" definition.
- **Trupel certificate of insurance (D8):**
  - The listed coverages meet the MSA §10.1 minimums: CGL $1M/$2M, tech E&O/cyber $5M, auto $1M and WC statutory.
  - The policies expire **March 1, 2027**. Diary a request for renewal certificates under MSA §10.2.
  - The certificate confers no rights, and Noubin is not an additional insured. Consider requiring additional-insured status in the amendment package.

## 5. Proposed Next Steps

1. **By November 13:** obtain October 2026 availability data and, if it shows a failure, serve the protective Chronic Failure notice (Issue 4). Consider a parallel MSA §12.3 breach notice.
2. **This week:** request written confirmation from Trupel that the October 19 notice is timely, or an extension. Review Trupel's November 13 remediation plan.
3. **Before any litigation step:** analyze forum strategy in light of SOW §10 (Issue 1).
4. Prepare an amendment package. Ideally use a Side Letter, given its top precedence under MSA §1.3. The package should cover:
   - deleting SOW §10 and SOW §6.2;
   - revising MSA §1.3, §3.4, §9, §11.3, §12.2 and §15.2.
5. Inventory Noubin's existing auction-technology vendors against MSA §3.4.

Please let me know if you would like me to draft the protective notice or the amendment package.

# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 12, 2026
**Re:** Noubin Auto Exchange, LLC / Trupel Lanecast, Inc.: Review of MSA and related documents

---

## I. Summary

I reviewed the eight documents in the folder:

- Master Services Agreement dated April 1, 2026 (**MSA**)
- Order Form No. 1 (**Order Form**)
- Service Level Schedule (**SLS**)
- Statement of Work (**SOW**)
- Side Letter dated October 26, 2026 (**Side Letter**)
- Term Sheet dated February 20, 2026 (**Term Sheet**)
- Ostrander Lot Sweeping Agreement
- Trupel's Certificate of Insurance

The last two are not relevant to the Trupel issues, as explained in Part IV.

One structural point drives several of the issues. **MSA §1.3** sets a "descending order of precedence": Side Letter, then Statement of Work, then Order Form, then Service Level Schedule, then MSA. It also states expressly that "if there is a conflict between the Statement of Work and this MSA, the Statement of Work shall prevail." The MSA therefore ranks *last*. Wherever Trupel's SOW departs from the MSA, the SOW controls.

**Items needing urgent attention:**

1. **Chronic Failure termination notice (Issue 1).** Noubin's October 19, 2026 notice appears to have been four days late. The stated termination date is January 15, 2027, and Trupel disputes the notice. Noubin needs a strategy now.
2. **Side Letter.** The Side Letter is still awaiting Noubin's countersignature. Trupel's remediation plan is due **tomorrow, November 13, 2026**. Noubin should not countersign until we settle the termination strategy. The reservation of rights in Side Letter §5 is helpful, but signing should be a deliberate choice.

---

## II. Issues

### Issue 1: Chronic Failure termination notice likely untimely (URGENT)

**Where:** SLS §6.2, read with Side Letter §§2.3–2.5.

**What it says:**

- SLS §6.1: a Chronic Failure occurs when Monthly Availability falls below 99.5% in three consecutive Measurement Periods.
- SLS §6.2: Noubin may then terminate, but its notice "must be delivered within fifteen (15) days after the end of the third consecutive Measurement Period."
- Side Letter §2.1: availability was 99.1% in July, 98.6% in August and 98.9% in September 2026, so a Chronic Failure occurred.
- The third failing month ended September 30, 2026. The window therefore closed **October 15, 2026**.
- Side Letter §2.3: Noubin delivered its notice on **October 19, 2026**, which is **four days late**.
- Side Letter §2.4: Trupel disputes timeliness and does not accept that the notice terminates the Agreement.
- Side Letter §2.5: Noubin maintains the notice is valid.

**Why it matters:** On the plain language, Noubin's Chronic Failure termination right has probably lapsed. SLS §6.3 gives significant benefits on a Chronic Failure termination: no termination fee, free transition assistance and payment of accrued credits. Noubin should not count on getting them. Noubin is planning to leave on January 15, 2027. If it stops performing or moves to another vendor on that basis and the notice is held ineffective, Noubin could itself be in breach. The risk is compounded by the 60-month term discussed in Issue 3.

The reservation of rights in Side Letter §5 keeps Noubin's position open, but it does not cure the late notice. MSA §16.3 requires any waiver to be in writing.

**Recommendations:**

- **Do not countersign the Side Letter as drafted** until we settle the strategy. If Noubin signs, add language confirming that acceptance of the Q3 credits is not a sole or exclusive remedy and is not an election of remedies. SLS §5.5 helps here, because it says credits do not limit SLS §6 or MSA §12.3.
- **Seek a written extension or waiver from Trupel.** Ask Trupel to agree that the October 19 notice is treated as timely, or to agree to a negotiated exit. Trupel's own Q3 failures and the remediation plan due November 13 give Noubin leverage.
- **Preserve alternative grounds.**
  - Serve a material-breach notice under **MSA §12.3** (30-day cure). The breaches include the Q3 availability failures and the apparent failure to meet the SOW §8.2 15-minute failover requirement (the July cause).
  - Request the monitoring records under SLS §7.2 and Side Letter §4.3.
  - Check whether October 2026 availability also fell below 99.5%. If it did, July through October contains a new run of three consecutive failing months (August, September, October). Its 15-day window would run to **November 15, 2026**, which is only days away. A fresh, timely Chronic Failure notice should be considered **immediately**.
- Diligence the facts of the October 19 delivery. Was there any earlier written communication (for example, at the quarterly business review) that could be argued to be notice?

---

### Issue 2: SOW chooses Georgia law and a Fulton County forum, and the SOW overrides the MSA

**Where:** SOW §10.1–10.2, read with MSA §1.3; compare MSA §14.1–14.2.

**What it says:**

- MSA §14.1–14.2 chooses Delaware law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the state or federal courts in New Castle County, Delaware. The Term Sheet (§11) agreed the same.
- SOW §10.1 provides that the SOW "and all claims arising out of or relating to the Services performed under it" are governed by "the laws of the State of Georgia."
- SOW §10.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to the courts "located in Fulton County, Georgia."
- MSA §1.3 says the Statement of Work prevails over the MSA. On its face, the Georgia clause therefore controls any claim tied to the Services.

**Why it matters:** The most likely disputes are platform outages, the current Chronic Failure fight and condition-report errors. All of these are "Services" claims. Noubin would have to litigate them in Trupel's home forum under Georgia law. MSA-level claims, such as data, confidentiality and fees, would stay in Delaware. That creates a real risk of split proceedings and arguments over which forum applies, which drives up cost and creates uncertainty. The Georgia clause also departs from the agreed Term Sheet.

**Recommendation:** Delete SOW §10 entirely. Alternatively, amend MSA §1.3 so that MSA §14 (along with §§9, 11 and 15) controls over any SOW, Order Form or Side Letter unless that document expressly identifies the MSA section it overrides. Given the live Chronic Failure dispute, we should also assess now which forum Trupel is likely to invoke.

---

### Issue 3: Automatic renewal for successive five-year terms with a narrow 30-day opt-out

**Where:** MSA §12.2, read with Order Form §3.

**What it says:**

- MSA §12.2 renews the Agreement automatically for successive renewal terms "each equal in length to the Initial Term."
- Non-renewal notice is effective only if delivered "not earlier than two hundred ten (210) days and not later than one hundred eighty (180) days" before expiry.
- The MSA does not state the Initial Term. Order Form §3 sets it at **sixty (60) months** from April 1, 2026, ending March 31, 2031.
- Read together, each renewal is another five years. The only exit is a 30-day window running roughly from early September to early October 2030.

**Why it matters:** If Noubin misses that one window, it is committed through March 2036, then again through 2041, and so on. A notice that is too early is also ineffective. The Term Sheet (§5.2) left renewal "to be agreed," so this mechanism was never negotiated. The risk is concrete given the Q3 2026 performance problems and the doubtful termination right in Issue 1.

**Recommendation:** Amend §12.2 so that renewals are for one-year terms, or occur only by mutual written agreement. Allow Noubin to give non-renewal notice at any time up to (say) 60–90 days before expiry, with no "not earlier than" limit. If the clause stays, docket the 2030 window now.

---

### Issue 4: Noubin's indemnity is uncapped and extends to Trupel's own condition reports

**Where:** SOW §6.2, read with MSA §9.2 and §11.3 (and §1.3).

**What it says:**

- MSA §9.2 requires Noubin to defend and indemnify Trupel against third-party claims arising out of "Consignor Content." MSA §1.1 defines that term as content supplied by or on behalf of Noubin or a Consignor.
- MSA §11.3 provides that the §11.1 cap (12 months' fees) and the §11.2 consequential damages exclusion "shall not apply to either party's obligations under Section 9."
- SOW §6.2 redefines Consignor Content, "for purposes of Section 9.2 of the MSA," to include all Vehicle Disclosures, "including condition reports prepared by Trupel Inspectors."
- SOW §2 defines Vehicle Disclosures to include odometer statements, title status and brand information, and frame and structural damage disclosures.
- Because the SOW prevails under MSA §1.3, the expanded definition controls.

**Why it matters:** Noubin would owe Trupel an **uncapped** indemnity for buyer arbitration, odometer, title-brand and damage-disclosure claims caused by **Trupel's own inspectors' errors**. Trupel's negligence would be shifted to Noubin without limit, while Trupel's own liability for poor condition reports would sit under the cap. This reverses the Term Sheet (§10.3), under which Noubin indemnifies only for content "supplied by Noubin or its consignors." Condition-report errors are a frequent source of wholesale-auction disputes, so this is a significant exposure.

**Recommendation:**

- Strike SOW §6.2, or limit it to content Noubin or Consignors actually supply.
- Add an express Trupel indemnity for third-party claims arising from Condition Report errors and inspector negligence.
- Make Noubin's §9.2 indemnity subject to a cap, or at minimum exclude from it any loss caused by Trupel's acts or omissions.

---

### Issue 5: Trupel may assign freely while Noubin cannot

**Where:** MSA §15.2; compare §15.1.

**What it says:**

- MSA §15.1 bars Noubin from assigning, including by merger or operation of law, without Trupel's prior written consent.
- MSA §15.2 provides that "Trupel may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without Noubin's consent to any person, upon written notice to Noubin."

**Why it matters:** Nothing prevents Trupel from assigning to a **competitor**, such as a rival auction operator or a platform owned by one. That assignee would then hold Noubin's Customer Data, including dealer buyer lists, consignor data, bid histories and pricing (MSA §1.1). The words "in part" also allow Trupel to split the Services between providers. Meanwhile, Noubin cannot even undergo a merger without Trupel's consent. That one-sided restriction could hinder a sale or reorganization of Noubin.

**Recommendation:**

- Make assignment mutual. Trupel should need Noubin's consent, with at most a carve-out for a successor to all or substantially all of Trupel's business that is **not a competitor** of Noubin.
- Give Noubin a right to terminate without fee if Trupel assigns to a competitor or undergoes a change of control.
- Carve Noubin's internal reorganizations and change-of-control transactions out of §15.1.
- Prohibit any partial assignment.

---

## III. Precedence: a cross-cutting fix

Several of the problems above arise because MSA §1.3 ranks the SOW and Side Letters above the MSA. Any later Side Letter (as Trupel drafts them) would rank above everything else. We recommend:
